rewards.title: What's in the machine?
rewards.body: Every asset here is a BNB Chain project, verified by contract address before it was ever added. Bridged versions of other chains' assets are deliberately left out.
rewards.priceNote: Prices are indicative and move constantly. They never influence what the machine drops — a spin resolves to a token amount, not a dollar amount.

page.title: Inside Bacha.
page.body: Every asset below was verified by contract address against three independent sources before it was added, and every percentage comes from the prize table a spin actually resolves against.
page.changes: The reward roster changes as the BNB ecosystem changes.
page.footnote: Prices are indicative and sourced from a cached third-party feed. They are never an input to settlement — a spin resolves to a fixed token amount, and what that amount is worth is a separate question the market answers.
page.priceUnavailable: Live pricing is unavailable right now, so prices are hidden rather than guessed.

fairness.body: Outcomes come from Chainlink VRF, not from us. The random word, the prize table it resolved against and the payout are all recorded onchain — so anyone can redo the maths and get the same answer.

page.title: Every spin has receipts.
page.body: Bacha does not ask you to believe the odds on the tin. The table, the randomness and the result are all recorded, and the maths that turns one into the other is four lines long.
page.tablesBody: These are the tables the machines resolve against. Every percentage here is computed from the same weights the contract holds — the UI has no separate copy of the odds to drift out of sync with.
page.methodBody: Prize selection is a weighted walk. Given a random word and a table, there is exactly one answer, and it does not depend on time, block number, balances or anything an operator controls.
page.methodNote: This mirrors BachaGame._selectPrize exactly. The verifier above runs the same walk in your browser and compares its answer to the recorded one.

one.title: You submit a spin.
one.body: Your wallet pays the tier price. In the same transaction the contract records who you are, which machine you used, and the exact prize table in force at that instant.

two.title: Its prize table is locked.
two.body: The spin is stamped with a machine version and the hash of that version's table. Published versions are append-only — there is no function in the contract that can edit one, so an operator changing odds afterwards cannot reach your spin.

three.title: Verifiable randomness settles it.
three.body: The contract asks Chainlink VRF for a random word. When it arrives, the callback walks the frozen weighted table and records exactly one prize. It writes storage and nothing else — no transfers, no outside calls.

four.title: The result is permanently recorded.
four.body: Random word, prize index, asset and amount are all emitted and stored. Anyone can replay the same maths and land on the same answer — this page does exactly that.

contracts.game: Tiers, prize tables, spins, randomness and claims.

verifier.label: Spin ID
verifier.idle: Every spin gets an id when it is paid for. Paste one here and this page will pull its record and re-derive the outcome independently.
verifier.pending: This spin has not settled yet. Its prize table is already locked, so the outcome cannot be influenced from here — the randomness simply has not arrived.
verifier.matched: Independently re-derived — this page reached the same result.
verifier.matchedDetail: Running the recorded random word through machine version {version}'s prize table in your browser produced entry #{index} — the same asset and amount the machine recorded.
verifier.mismatched: Re-derivation did not match the recorded result.
verifier.mismatchedDetail: The recorded reward differs from what this table produces for that random word. Treat this result as unverified and report it.
verifier.notFound: That spin could not be found.
verifier.unreachable: Could not reach the verifier. Try again in a moment.

story.body: Capsule machines have worked the same way for fifty years: you pay, the drum turns, something comes out. Bacha keeps the mechanism and replaces the drum with a contract you can read.

ageGate.bodyOne: Bacha is a game with randomised outcomes. A spin costs money and what comes out is worth whatever the market says it is worth — which may be less than you paid.
